This patient is a 46-year-old male who presents with chronic abdominal pain, constipation, and occasional diarrhea. It seems to get a little better when I have a bowel movement. Doctor: Have you undergone any prior medical evaluations, such as imaging studies, blood tests, or consultations with specialists, related to your abdominal pain, constipation, or diarrhea? Patient: Yes, I had an abdominal CT scan a few months ago, and they said it looked normal. I haven't had any other tests or consultations for this issue before today. Doctor: Could you provide more details about your dietary patterns, including any specific foods that seem to trigger your symptoms, and whether you have noticed any weight loss, rectal bleeding, or changes in your appetite? Patient: I don't have any rectal bleeding, and my appetite is normal. I do notice that certain foods, like pasta with creamy sauce, seem to trigger my diarrhea, and I've had some issues with constipation as well. My weight has been pretty stable, though I could stand to lose about 25 pounds. Patient: No, I haven't had any stool tests like fecal calprotectin or occult blood tests. I didn't even know those were options until today.
